thread:
jamie: Quick check — we need to pick the operational model for customer-initiated peering when we separate the control plane into a private VPC. Two options on the table: 1) cross-account VPC peering that the customer accepts (direct route), 2) outbound relay (our egress agents/proxy) so no peering required. Thinking in terms of least-privilege, auditability, and support cost. Thoughts?

alex: +1 on surfacing the tradeoffs. Peering = lower latency/cost but higher blast radius and customer has to accept routes. Relay = more ops work for us but simpler from customer's network side (outbound only).

sara: Security angle: peering gives two-way network reachability unless we carefully restrict route tables/security groups. Hard to guarantee zero inbound path mistakes across cloud providers/accounts. If we do peering we need an automated verification (route + sg audit) and explicit acceptance flow documented.

mike: For Dedicated customers we already do reserved peering in some cases. Problem is support tickets where a customer accidentally overlaps CIDR and breaks routing. That suggests we need a safe default that fails open/closed? I'd prefer fail-closed for control plane (deny unless verified).

jamie: Agree on fail-closed. What about a hybrid: allow peering but only for specific control-plane subnets + deny routes to data plane ranges. We could require customers to accept a signed CSR/manifest from us that enumerates allowed prefixes and an acceptance token.

infra-bot: FYI: previous spike showed we can restrict route propagation via explicit route tables and prefix-lists, but enforcement differs across clouds (aws supports prefix lists, gcp has different semantics).

sec-bot: Checklist suggestion: 1) customer acceptance token, 2) automated post-peering audit, 3) runtime egress-only failover path if audit fails.

sara: The acceptance token is nice. Also add 'short TTL audit logs' — proof the customer accepted on X timestamp with a hash of the manifest. That helps for compliance and incident triage.

alex: Operational notes: implement a small state machine -- REQUESTED -> PEER_CREATED -> AUDIT_PASSED -> ACTIVE. If AUDIT_FAILED mark PEER_QUARANTINED and bring up relay fallback automatically. Simple UI buttons for SRE/SE to re-run audit.

jamie: Example minimal manifest: 
```json
{
  "version": 1,
  "customer_account": "123456789012",
  "allowed_controlplane_prefixes": ["10.50.0.0/24"],
  "accepted_at": "<timestamp>",
  "acceptance_token": "<signed-by-customer>"
}
```

mike: One more thing — cost modeling. Peering shifts network egress costs to customer in many clouds; relay pushes egress onto us. We should add a billing flag customers opt into when they pick peering so sales doesn't get surprise charges.

jamie: Agreed. UX: in onboarding flow present clear checkbox: "I consent to cross-account peering for control plane (may affect my egress billing)" + show estimated cost delta.

infra-bot: Implementation gotchas: must handle overlapping CIDRs gracefully (reject with clear error), and automate NAT/route cleanup on deletion. Also rotate acceptance manifests when we change control plane prefix layout.

alex: For rolling upgrades we also want canarying: start with peering to a canary control-plane subnet, run audit & metrics for 24h, then expand. That reduces blast radius.

jamie: Sounds like a plan. Next actions: (1) draft acceptance manifest spec + signing flow (jamie), (2) state machine + UI mock for onboarding & quarantine (alex), (3) audit rules + cloud-specific enforcement doc (sara), (4) fallback relay cost model (mike). I'll create a short RFC PR by EOD and link a spike for prefix-list enforcement per-cloud. @sara @alex @mike ping if you want to pair on the PR. :thumbsup:

sec-bot: Security note — make sure acceptance_token uses KMS/HSM-backed keys and we store only the signed blob (not raw private keys).

mike: ok, filing support playbook item: "What to do if peer stuck in PEER_QUARANTINED". Will include CLI commands and console steps.

jamie: thanks everyone. Follow-ups in PR  — closing this thread for now.

infra-bot: deploy-bot: created issue INFRA-7243 for the peering state machine spike.
